title: Disappointed by Zoomers
summary: Long rant diagnosing Gen Z through 'three Cs' (cringe, cope, clout) plus algorithms and zoomer humor. NH blames the environment built by millennials and boomers, and links it to drug/SARM culture, supplement marketing and the decline of YouTube fitness. He closes by urging young viewers to drop irony and addictions and become adults and role models.
claims: Zoomers' shortcomings are the product of an environment created by millennials and boomers; NH blames his own generation
Gen Z's pathology rests on three Cs: cringe, cope and clout
Shame is a useful social tool, but cringe culture turns it against risk-taking and trying, making it the ultimate weapon of conformity
Teenagers are deeply conformist, and zoomers never move past the groupthink stage to stand on their own
Millennials became burnt-out tryhards from a boomer work ethic; zoomers reacted by making trying itself uncool
Zoomers only like things ironically to be bulletproof against mockery, but doing something ironically is the first step to doing it unironically
Calling any attempt to see the bright side 'cope' reflects a nihilism zoomers are born into, cheerful rather than depressed
People who hate self-improvement avoid it because accepting it means admitting there was a problem in the first place
Zoomers normalize and celebrate mental illness instead of fighting it, so it stays with them
An adult is someone with responsibility; cringe and cope remove responsibility, producing a Peter Pan generation
Young people are the top demographic for addiction and take SARMs and other PEDs as casually as candy; NH expects them to be hit hardest by PED harm
SARM, pre-workout and test-booster companies use flashy childish marketing aimed at zoomers' arrested development
Viewers who quit stimulants for two weeks after his caffeine video reported their headaches, fatigue and shaking disappeared
Early exposure to social media and porn will make healthy male-female relationships and birth rates collapse
Zoomers worship influencers and outsource their decisions, asking NH what to do instead of trying things themselves
YouTube fitness degraded because the algorithm mirrors young viewers' clicks, pushing short content and shrinking attention spans; viewers say his long videos retrained their focus
Supplement and pre-workout companies target zoomers as the most gullible demographic, spending their parents' money
Corporate capitalism wants consumers kept in permanent adolescence because adults consume less
Virtuous role models have been removed for young men, leaving influencers barely older than their audience
Morality is not innate; without guidance people gravitate toward drugs because they feel good
Zoomer humor is deliberately unfunny and is in truth a cry for help, an absurdist response to a meaningless world
Freedom is found in restrictions; Gen Z is the freest generation yet still in chains
Young viewers should break free of irony and of stimulant, video game and social media addictions to become adults and role models for the next generation
